audience_question: Which shuttle option meets the minimum range at the lowest upfront cost?
fit_rationale: The question asks how four options differ on the same criteria against a threshold. An aligned matrix keeps every option's exact range and cost with units in the row labels, shows the 200 km minimum as a Yes/No row, and lets the reader check the answer across one column. A single-measure bar chart would drop the units and the threshold check, and the question depends on two measures at once.
tradeoff: The matrix keeps all exact values, but the reader must scan across rows to confirm the answer rather than seeing a single ranked bar. The Alder column is marked with shading and a text label rather than a ranking, so the matrix does not imply Alder is best on every criterion.
caveats: All figures are fictional planning estimates from one procurement worksheet; no uncertainty ranges were provided.
Annual energy cost assumes 18,000 km of service per vehicle per year and excludes maintenance and charging-infrastructure costs.
The brief does not state whether upfront cost is per vehicle or for the whole fleet.
Alder meets the 200 km minimum by 10 km (210 km against 200 km).
Cedar has the lowest upfront cost (35 thousand USD) but its 190 km range does not meet the minimum.
Alder is not the lowest on annual energy cost; Birch (3.9) and Dogwood (3.8) are lower than Alder (4.2) in thousands of USD.
